author: original (NevaIB)
title: Presenting data

points.text: Cumulative frequency graphs: median, quartiles, percentiles, range, IQR

bigPicture: Graphs show the shape of a data set at a glance. Cumulative frequency graphs and box plots turn that shape into medians, quartiles and comparisons.

keyIdeas.answer: Group the data into classes and record frequencies. A histogram has touching bars for continuous data; in SL the classes have equal width, so bar height = frequency.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you read a cumulative frequency graph?
keyIdeas.answer: Plot cumulative frequency at each upper class boundary and join with a smooth curve. Median at n/2, Q1 at n/4, Q3 at 3n/4, the pth percentile at p% of n; IQR = Q3 − Q1.

keyIdeas.cue: What does a box-and-whisker diagram show?
keyIdeas.answer: Minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum, with outliers marked separately and the whisker ending at the most extreme non-outlier. Compare distributions by median (centre) and IQR (spread).

keyTerms.def: the top edge of a class, where cumulative frequency is plotted
value below which a given percentage of the data lie

workedExamples.title: Read a CF graph
workedExamples.prompt: n = 80. Which cumulative frequencies give the median, Q1, Q3 and the 90th percentile?
steps: median at 40, Q1 at 20, Q3 at 60

misconceptions.wrong: Plot cumulative frequency at class midpoints
The longer box half has more data
misconceptions.right: Each quarter of a box plot holds 25% of the data, whatever its length.

practice.prompt: A box plot shows minimum 4, Q1 = 10, median 15, Q3 = 19 and maximum 30. Find the IQR and determine whether 30 is an outlier.
Times t (minutes): 0 < t ≤ 10: 5; 10 < t ≤ 20: 12; 20 < t ≤ 30: 18; 30 < t ≤ 40: 10; 40 < t ≤ 50: 5. Write down the cumulative frequencies and estimate the median.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
